title: Make VCF Operations for Networks application onboarding safe to retry
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsNetworksApp/VcfOpsNetworksApp.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that onboards an application into VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 Operations for Networks, the successor to vRealize Network Insight. An inventory pipeline re-runs this onboarding step every time a workload domain is re-scanned, and the create route documents no conflict response, so a second run silently produces a second application under the same name. The call must be safe to repeat.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. That focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-for-networks-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. This is the VCF Operations for Networks API on the `/api/ni` base path, not the separate VCF Operations `/suite-api` specification sitting in the same directory of that repository. The only operationIds in scope are `create`, `getSavedApplicationsSummaries`, `addApplicationWithTiers` and `delete`, issued in that order; contact no other route.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` version `13.5.0.25380678` as an environment prerequisite. Keep that genuine external module prerequisite in the protected manifest and in the module's `Import-Module`. The generated SDK ships no cmdlets for the `/api/ni` surface, so issue these four requests yourself with PowerShell's built-in web cmdlets, building each route from the specification's `/api/ni` base path. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, specifications or harness tools.

Preserve and export only:

`New-VcfOpsNetworksApplication -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> -Name <string> -Tier <hashtable[]> [-Protocol <https|http>] [-Port <int>] [-DomainType <LOCAL|LDAP>] [-DomainValue <string>] [-EnableIntent <bool>] [-LastModifiedTimestamp <long>] [-PageSize <int>]`

`Protocol` defaults to `https`, `Port` to 443, `DomainType` to `LOCAL` and `PageSize` to 100. Each `-Tier` hashtable carries `Name` plus at least one of `VmFilter`, a search expression, and `IpAddress`, a string array; reject any other key. Raise an `ArgumentException` before any traffic for a blank or surrounding-whitespace `Server`, `Name` or tier `Name`, an empty `-Tier` array, a repeated tier name, or an `LDAP` domain with no `DomainValue`.

Wire contract:

1. `create` opens the session. Send `username`, `password` and `domain` in that order. `domain` carries `domain_type`; the specification notes that `value` is not required for a `LOCAL` domain, so send `value` only for `LDAP`. This is the one operation that carries no `Authorization` header.
2. Every later request presents the issued token exactly once as `Authorization: NetworkInsight <token>`. The prefix is `NetworkInsight`, not `Bearer`.
3. `getSavedApplicationsSummaries` is the existence probe. Request the first page with `size` only, then follow the `cursor` the node hands back, sending `size` then `cursor`, until a page arrives without one. Never send `modifiedAfter`, `fetch_member_counts` or `fetch_update_status`. Stop as soon as a returned application's `name` equals `-Name` exactly and case-sensitively; that application is the result, and `addApplicationWithTiers` must not be reached at all.
4. `addApplicationWithTiers` runs only when the probe found nothing. Its route ends in a trailing slash exactly as the specification spells it. Send `name`, then `enable_intent` only when the caller bound `-EnableIntent`, then `tiers` in the caller's order. Each tier sends `name` then `group_membership_criteria`; a `VmFilter` becomes a `SearchMembershipCriteria` entry over entity type `VirtualMachine`, an `IpAddress` list becomes an `IPAddressMembershipCriteria` entry, and a tier carrying both sends the search entry first. Each criteria object carries `membership_type` and only its own criteria member. Note that the enum spells the address variant `IPAddressMembershipCriteria` while the member it selects is `ip_address_membership_criteria`.
5. `-LastModifiedTimestamp`, when bound, becomes the `If-Match` header. The specification types that header as a bare int64, not as a quoted entity tag.
6. `delete` releases the token. The specification caps a user at 100 valid tokens and advises deleting a token after use, so it must run on every path, including after an earlier step failed.

Optional members the caller did not supply must be absent from the request rather than sent as `null`, `""`, `[]` or `{}`. That covers `entity_id`, `source_group_entity_id` and `enable_intent` on the application, `entity_id`, `member_list` and `source_group_entity_id` on each tier, `value` on a `LOCAL` domain, the unrequested probe query parameters, and the `If-Match` header.

Return one `[pscustomobject]` carrying exactly `Name`, `EntityId`, `EntityType`, `Created`, `Source`, `TierCount`, `MemberCount`, `LastModifiedTime`, `PagesScanned` and `TierNames`. `Created` is `$true` only when this call issued `addApplicationWithTiers`, and `Source` is `created` or `existing` to match. `TierCount`, `MemberCount` and `LastModifiedTime` come from the application the node reports, whether it was found or created; `PagesScanned` counts the probe requests this call made; `TierNames` lists the caller's tier names in order. Never emit the password or the session token.

A reply from a loopback fixture is test scaffolding, not evidence about any real deployment. Contact no live VMware endpoint.
